samples.question: What uptime SLA does the Pro plan include?
samples.answer: The Pro plan includes a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for the HTTPS edge and managed PostgreSQL primary.
samples.ground_truth: Pro includes a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for the HTTPS edge and managed PostgreSQL primary.
context_texts: Pro includes a 99.9% monthly uptime SLA for the HTTPS edge and managed PostgreSQL primary. SLA credits are 10% of the monthly subscription for each 0.1% of downtime below 99.9%, capped at 50% of that month's subscription. Scheduled maintenance windows published 72 hours in advance do not count as downtime.

Enterprise includes a 99.99% monthly uptime SLA, a 15-minute Sev-1 page-out, and a named customer success manager. SLA credits follow the same 10% per 0.1% miss schedule as Pro, capped at 100% of the monthly subscription.

Starter includes 2 vCPU / 4 GB RAM application instances, 20 GB object storage, and 50,000 API requests per calendar month. Support is email-only with a next-business-day target. Starter has no uptime SLA.

Starter email support is monitored Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00 in the workspace home region's local time, excluding public holidays. Pro adds 24x5 chat. Enterprise includes 24x7 chat and phone, plus a dedicated Slack Connect channel.

samples.question: How do I request a refund and what is the monthly refund window?
subqueries: How do I request a refund?
What is the monthly refund window?
samples.answer: To request a refund, go to the billing console under **Settings → Billing → Request refund** or email `billing@nimbus.example` from an owner account. Include the workspace id and invoice number. The monthly refund window is 14 days from the first paid invoice if API request volume is under 10,000.
samples.ground_truth: Request a refund in Settings → Billing → Request refund or email billing@nimbus.example from an owner account with workspace id and invoice number. Monthly subscriptions may be refunded in full within 14 days of the first paid invoice if API volume is under 10,000.
context_texts: Refunds are requested in the billing console under **Settings → Billing → Request refund**, or by emailing `billing@nimbus.example` from an owner account. The request must include the workspace id (`ws_...`) and the invoice number. Finance replies within 2 business days. Approved refunds settle to the original payment method within 5–10 business days.

Monthly subscriptions may be refunded in full if cancellation is requested within 14 days of the first paid invoice and API request volume is under 10,000 for that workspace. Annual subscriptions may be refunded pro-rata within 30 days of purchase, minus any consumed overage charges.

Opening a chargeback while a refund request is open automatically pauses the refund. Workspaces with two or more chargebacks in 12 months are ineligible for self-serve refunds and must go through Enterprise legal review.

Subscriptions are billed monthly in arrears on the workspace anniversary date. Adding seats mid-cycle is prorated. Removing seats takes effect at the next renewal. Invoices are issued as PDF to billing contacts and are due in 15 days.

samples.question: Which regions can Starter and Pro choose and can the home region be changed later?
subqueries: Which regions can Starter and Pro choose?
Can the home region be changed later?
samples.answer: Starter and Pro workspaces may choose `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, or `ap-southeast-1` at creation time. The home region cannot be changed later.
samples.ground_truth: Starter and Pro may choose us-east-1, eu-west-1, or ap-southeast-1 at creation. The home region cannot be changed later.
context_texts: Starter and Pro workspaces may choose `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, or `ap-southeast-1` at creation time. The home region cannot be changed later. Enterprise can add `eu-central-1` and `ap-northeast-1`. Object storage replicas stay inside the same geopolitical area: US, EU, or APAC. Backups never leave that area.

Starter is limited to 10 requests per second (RPS) per workspace. Pro is limited to 100 RPS. Enterprise default is 500 RPS and can be raised with a support ticket. Burst tokens equal 2x the sustained RPS for 10 seconds. HTTP 429 responses include `Retry-After` in seconds.
Data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or newer. Data at rest uses AES-256. Customer-managed keys (CMK) are available on Enterprise via AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault in the workspace home region.

Application logs are retained 14 days on Starter, 30 days on Pro, and 90 days on Enterprise. Audit logs are retained 1 year on Pro and 7 years on Enterprise. Deleted workspaces enter a 30-day recoverable tombstone, then are cryptographically erased.
